parsed.explanation: Documented trans-specific enforcement makes same-sex criminalisation an active lever: police arbitrarily arrest and sometimes assault trans people, a trans woman was convicted under s.153 and served eight years in a men's prison, and the constitutional court upheld 14-year plus corporal provisions in 2024. Arrest foreseeably triggers forced stripping, medical exams, extortion, neighbour violence and public outing, with no effective remedy after the moratorium annulment. No capital punishment or custody deaths are documented, so risk sits above the 0.15 anchor but well below 0.25.

entry_documents.interaction: No border, passport-marker or screening rules are sourced; any document check could expose the traveller to the documented penal-code enforcement, but that interaction is uncertain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arbitrary arrest and detention of trans people, sometimes with assault; trans woman sentenced to eight years and served in men's prison; another to 14 years; forced stripping and medical examinations after arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under ss.153-156 is the gateway to custody, extortion, forced exams and misgendered imprisonment; moratorium was annulled and police circumvented it.

care_services.exposure: Medical staff denied services on gender-expression grounds; trans man beaten then refused treatment; nurses mocked patients presenting for HIV tests.
care_services.interaction: Denial of care compounds police violence and arrest-related forced medical examinations.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Ss.153,154,156 criminalise consensual same-sex conduct up to 14 years with corporal punishment, upheld 28 June 2024; organisation reports gender-nonconforming people most likely targeted; senior officials, party and religious figures voice hostility, including calls to kill gay people with impunity after prosecution discontinued.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2019 broadcasting hate-speech regulation is media-specific only; enforcement not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing and failed accountability license police and community enforcement against visibly trans visitors.

minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. No age-specific rule is sourced; guardian detention would have family consequences but this is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Arrested men had house ransacked, were assaulted by neighbours, threatened with burning alive, extorted by community police, stripped and photographed for social media; bail denied in 2009 citing public anger, magistrate said sentencing protected society.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police/community-police action and neighbour violence follow discovery, showing police worsen rather than protect victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Constitutional challenge dismissed 2024 leaving reform to legislature with no documented action; moratorium annulled 2016; hate-speech prosecution discontinued; no broad anti-discrimination protection.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal court process confirmed criminalisation rather than providing recourse, making paper protections ineffective.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: imprisonment under morality law, detention abuse, delayed/ineffective courts. Higher than 0.15-B because no capital provision, custody deaths or systematic custodial beatings are documented here, and no border-detention regime is sourced.

Lower than 0.25-C: both have birth-sex/men's prison placement and slow remedies, but here sentences of 8-14 years, documented police assault of trans people, and 2024 court upholding criminalisation show imprisonment is not merely brief or rare.

Well below 0.35-B: that anchor has stops, confiscation and fines with detention rarely becoming imprisonment; here documented trans convictions and 14-year maximum, plus forced exams and extortion on arrest, are materially more severe.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national penal law, upheld in 2024, is enforced by police who target gender-nonconforming people, circumvent suspensions, and whose arrests trigger community-police extortion, forced stripping/medical exams, neighbour violence and men's-prison custody. Medical denial and visible official hostility remove mitigation. No protective subnational regime, entry rule or remedy is documented to counter this. Uncertainty about border screening does not reduce the documented post-outing exposure; with a minor, no age-specific protection is documented. The operative risk is long imprisonment after outing, without documented execution.
